v1.feedback: The calyx inversion is a genuine trickster move — form-level surprise, not just a color gimmick. Final on-screen palette reads as terracotta/dusty-indigo on cream, which is restrained despite the raw light uniforms (warmC, coolC) sitting near ~70% HSL saturation; the lighting math mutes them correctly. Two improvements: (1) the 18s cycle with 3s hold may feel metronomic — consider randomizing the interval ±5s so the trick feels spontaneous rather than clockwork, and (2) the scattered particle sparkle during inversion risks reading as noise if overdone — clamp its contribution to ≤0.08 additive and tie it to petal-edge vNR so it reads as structural refraction rather than random glitter.

Two refinements: the Lorenz-inspired surface flow adds drift but doesn't produce a recognizable attractor shape — consider naming it honestly as 'chaotic perturbation' or actually routing particles along a projected Lorenz orbit for veining. The Riley wave interference (rowW/colW) at these frequencies may make the surface read as corrugated rather than organic petal tissue — try halving uRowFreq/uColFreq or replacing with a smoother radial falloff so the calyx curvature reads cleanly at rest, letting the inversion moment carry the visual drama.
